note: THE SAME RULE FOR `^', whose anchoring contexts are the mirror image: the START of the regexp, or just after `\\(', `\\(?:' or `\\|'. Emacs answers (0 nil 0): "a^b" matches the literal text "a^b", refuses "ab", and a `^' in the middle of a group is a literal too. kg answers (nil nil nil). Recorded separately from the `$' case because the contexts are different lists and an implementation can get one right and the other wrong.
